messages:
sam: Heads-up 1 proposal on diff context expansion for Prompt Evals. Link to proto + recording: https://files.redwood/s/diff-context-proto. Main asks: microcopy for the expand control, keyboard shortcut for expand/collapse all, SR behavior when context is revealed, and perf tradeoffs for prefetch vs on-demand. Need consensus before we freeze the scorecard row.

elaine: In the mock the control is a chevron with tooltip 'Show context'. UX nit: chevrons alone are ambiguous. Suggest visible text 'Show context' on hover for clarity or replace with a small button: "Show context" / "Hide context". Also consider shortening to "Context" if space is tight.

jon: Implementation thoughts: on-demand fetch for expanded context avoids initial payload bloat. Prefetching the first 3 rows on page load could reduce perceived latency for heavy scrolling. Also watch DOM size if many rows are expanded simultaneously.

aria: A11y concerns:
- The expand button must have aria-expanded="false"/"true" and an accessible label like 'Show context for result 5'. Don't rely on visual proximity.
- When content is inserted, move focus policy: do not auto-focus into expanded content (disorienting). Instead, ensure the expanded content is reachable via Tab and announce via aria-live polite: 'Context loaded for result 5'.
- Provide a skip link at top of scorecard to jump to next collapsed diff or to expanded content region.

maya: UXR: users want quick peek into surrounding prompt + model answer. They also liked 'Expand all for page' when doing batch triage. But expand-all on large pages caused jank in tests. Recommendation: provide 'Expand visible' (only expands items currently in viewport) as a compromise.

elaine: Copy options for the control: full label 'Show context' / 'Hide context' (clear), short label 'Context' tooltip (compact), and icon-only with aria-label (minimal). My pick: text button 'Show context' for desktop rows, icon+text for compact rows.

sam: Decisions so far:
1) Use textual toggle: 'Show context' / 'Hide context' as primary for desktop; compact rows use icon+aria-label.
2) Add keyboard shortcut: C = toggle focused row context. Add global shortcut: Shift+C = expand visible (viewport) items. Shortcuts registered only when scorecard focused.
3) Accessibility: expand button must have aria-expanded and an accessible name; announce 'Context loaded for result N' via aria-live polite; do NOT auto-focus into inserted content.
4) Prefetch: prefetch for the first 3 rows only; all other expansions fetch on demand. Provide an opt-in setting for aggressive prefetch for power users.

jon: I'll implement the aria-expanded attributes and the scoped shortcut handlers. For expand-visible, I'll use IntersectionObserver to pick viewport rows and then batch fetch their contexts to avoid spiky network load. I'll also add a CSS class to collapse expanded content visually without reflow (use max-height transitions) to reduce jank.

aria: I'll add these a11y checks to the test plan:
- Verify aria-expanded and accessible name per row
- Confirm aria-live announces text when context finishes loading
- Ensure Tab order reaches expanded content after expansion
- Validate no auto-focus into new content

elaine: I'll update the Figma with desktop + compact variants, the 'Expand visible' control in the top toolbar, and tooltip copy. Also will add an in-UI hint for keyboard shortcuts: 'C toggles context' in the help panel. ETA: EOD.

maya: I'll run a quick moderated test tomorrow focusing on perceived latency for on-demand vs prefetched rows and the discoverability of the 'Expand visible' control.

uploader-bot: uploaded files: diff_context_v1.png, expand_visible_proto.html (https://files.redwood/s/diff-context-proto)

sam: Thanks all. Action items: @elaine update mocks, @jon spike IntersectionObserver + batch prefetch, @aria update a11y test plan, @maya run quick UXR check. Flag any blockers before sprint planning. :thumbsup:
